status: Written and pushed before any stage-80 code or run. Design choices approved by the owner on 28 November 2026: an NVIDIA L4 (not an A100, which is not available on the owner's plan), so the stage stays directly comparable with stages 76-79; no separate timing test, the run's own calibration sets the number of filter updates N_M per pool size, so every cell is at exact equal cost; 24 seeds; one primary contrast (E_count) at 95%; no random_once arm; extra checkpoints for the filter and random arms; the 24 seeds run as two pre-registered blocks of 12, with resumption on another L4 allowed; the seed count is fixed at 24 and no outcome is read between blocks.
question: With every cell at exact equal cost (the filter's update count N_M set from this run's own calibration for each pool size M), does doubling the number of useful (in-format QA) chunks at a fixed share still increase the equal-cost advantage of the one-pass offline filter over random selection?
motivation: Stage 79 found E_count = -0.083 [-0.141, -0.010] (97.5%, 5/6 seeds) with N = 1633 and B = 3000 fixed in every cell. Scoring a 4096-chunk pool costs about half as much as scoring an 8192-chunk pool, so in the M = 4096 cells the filter left about 730 charged steps unused. When the M = 4096 cells were put at exact equal cost by shortening the random arm to B_eq(4096) = 2366, E_count was -0.047 [-0.116, +0.035], so the count effect rested partly on the filter's unused budget. Stage 79 had six seeds. This stage removes the unused budget in the other direction (the filter spends all of B in every cell, with N_M per pool size) and uses 24 seeds, so that the count effect is tested at exact equal cost with about half the stage-79 interval width.

factor.fixed: As stage 79: trained model Qwen2.5-1.5B and proxy Qwen2.5-0.5B with the stage-76/78/79 numerics, LoRA (rank 8, alpha 16, q_proj and v_proj) and AdamW (lr 5e-4, weight decay 0); scorer gradient alignment with the 120 All/dev probe at the seed's initial adapter (experiments.llm_web_filter.score, align_grad, batch 16); B = 3000 random-step costs in every cell; chunk length 65 tokens; the four stage-79 pools unchanged.
factor.changed_from_stage_79: (1) N is no longer fixed: N_M = floor(B - S(M) / c_r + 1e-9) per pool size from this run's calibration, so the filter's scoring plus training equals B in every cell (from the stage-79 calibration, about 1574 at M = 8192 and about 2268 at M = 4096). (2) 24 seeds instead of 6. (3) No random_once arm. (4) One primary contrast at 95% instead of two co-primaries at 97.5%. (5) Extra checkpoints at equal charged cost for both arms. (6) Two pre-registered blocks of 12 seeds.
factor.identity: Q = M x s, so only two of the three quantities vary independently. Pool size per se is not separated from count or share. In addition, N_M differs between the pool sizes by design (exact equal cost), so at M = 4096 the filter trains about 700 more updates than at M = 8192, on a kept set that holds about 55% of its pool. E_count therefore compares the filter at exact equal cost, not at equal update count; this is the intended comparison and is stated as part of the scope.

data.pools: Exactly the four stage-79 pools, rebuilt by the stage-79 code (experiments.llm_count_share_filter) from the same QA subsets (Q1024 from stage 78; Q512 = default_rng(7901); Q256 = default_rng(7902)), the same web lists and the same layout. Each pool digest must equal the stage-79 journaled digest (results/llm-count-share-filter-journal.jsonl, calibration.population), else abort. Cell d also equals the stage-78 Q1024 pool. No new ArabicMMLU item is trained; no new FineWeb-2 chunk enters any pool.

target.items: 512 new ArabicMMLU All/test items, never evaluated or trained in this project. Eligible rows: (1) not in any earlier evaluation set: the 3,328 rows excluded in stage 79 (the 2,816 of experiments.llm_supply_filter.excluded_rows plus the 512 stage-78 target IDs) plus the 512 stage-79 target IDs journaled in results/llm-count-share-filter-journal.jsonl, 3,840 rows; abort if the count differs; (2) not one of the 4,946 IDs used for training (data/evaluation_status.json, stage_74.used_for_training); (3) clean under criteria (a)-(e) of stage 75 (experiments.llm_once_filter.target_candidates, unchanged), with criterion (e) applied to the four pools as trained plus the 4,946 items tokenized in the training template. Counts journaled; abort if fewer than 512 rows are eligible. Target = sort(eligible[default_rng(8022).choice(len(eligible), 512, replace=False)]) in row order. Used for evaluation only; exposed after this stage.
target.expected_eligible: About 3,800 (4,308 in stage 79 minus its 512 targets). Not a decision criterion.
target.exposure_status: Confirmatory: the target items are unexposed before this stage (checked against data/evaluation_status.json and the journals of stages 73-79), so project rule 8 is met.
target.format: Cloze item loss and accuracy exactly as stages 73-79 (experiments.llm_web_filter.evaluate) with the 1.5B model. Step 0 (LoRA B = 0, identical for every run) is evaluated once per seed, in that seed's first random run, and must be identical across seeds and machines.

design.seeds: 24 seeds, 38000 to 38023. Block 1 = seeds 38000-38011; block 2 = seeds 38012-38023. The seed count is fixed at 24 and does not depend on any outcome.
design.calibration: Once, before block 1 and before any target evaluation, seed 80999: c_r = median of steps 5-24 of 24 random 1.5B steps on the cell-d pool; S(8192) = wall-clock of complete 0.5B proxy scoring of the cell-d pool; S(4096) = the same on the cell-b pool. Journaled. N_8192 = floor(B - S(8192) / c_r + 1e-9); N_4096 = floor(B - S(4096) / c_r + 1e-9). Abort before any run and report if N_8192 is outside [1417, 1731] (1574 +/- 10%), if N_4096 is outside [2041, 2495] (2268 +/- 10%), or if N_4096 <= N_8192. N_8192 and N_4096 are fixed for the whole stage, both blocks and any resumption included; they are never re-estimated.
design.cost_points: Three equal charged-cost points C in {2400, 2700, 3000} random-step costs. The random arm at cost C has trained C updates. The filter at cost C has trained k_M(C) = N_M - (3000 - C) updates (scoring charged as S(M) / c_r = 3000 - N_M); for example about 974, 1274, 1574 at M = 8192 and about 1668, 1968, 2268 at M = 4096 with the stage-79 calibration.

arms.random: Each step a chunk drawn uniformly with replacement from the cell's pool; 3000 updates; evaluated at 2400, 2700 and 3000 (and at 0 in the seed's first random run).
arms.align05_once: Score the cell's pool with the 0.5B proxy at the seed's initial adapter (proxy freed before the 1.5B model is loaded); keep the N_M highest scores (ties to the lower index); train the 1.5B model on the kept chunks once each in random order; N_M updates; evaluated at k_M(2400), k_M(2700) and N_M. The full scoring time is journaled.

design.schedule: Per seed and pool size: rng = default_rng(seed); in this order rand = rng.integers(M, size=3000); once = rng.permutation(N_M). align05_once trains kept[once], random trains rand. Cells with the same M and seed share the schedule and differ only in pool content.
design.run_order: Seeds in order; within seed index i (0 to 23), cells in the order (a, b, c, d) rotated left by i mod 4; within each cell, arms (random, align05_once) rotated left by i mod 2.
design.measurement: As stage 79. Per run: losses and accuracies at the checkpoints, step seconds, adapter digest at step 50, views per training-set chunk (max and mean). Per align05_once run: all M scores, kept indices and digest, QA share and QA count of the kept set, scoring seconds. Per random run: QA chunks drawn and distinct QA chunks seen at 2400, 2700 and 3000.
design.coverage: 24 seeds x 4 cells x 2 arms = 192 runs plus one calibration; 96 runs per block.

blocks.definition: Block 1 runs the calibration and seeds 38000-38011 (96 runs); block 2 runs seeds 38012-38023 (96 runs) with the block-1 calibration. Each block is planned as one session of about 12 hours (time_estimate).
blocks.machines: Both blocks run on an NVIDIA L4. Block 2, or a resumption within either block, may run on another L4: the runner re-verifies population, pools, target and schedule digests, journals the new environment (device, driver, software versions), re-evaluates step 0 for the first seed it runs, and continues with the journaled calibration. A device other than an L4 aborts. A short re-timing (24 random steps, as the calibration) is journaled on each new machine for description only; it never changes N_8192 or N_4096.
blocks.blinding: No loss, accuracy or contrast is printed, read, summarized or reported between blocks. The runner prints only progress counts and checks; the interim backups on colab/stage80-journal hold the journal but are not opened for outcomes. Between blocks only the audit items that do not involve outcomes may be checked (run counts, digests, environment, step-0 identity). The analysis is run once, after all 192 runs and the audit.
blocks.incomplete_stage: If block 2 cannot be completed for external reasons (no L4 available, plan ended), the reason is documented in research/llm-exact-cost-count-deviations.md before any outcome is read; the completed seeds are then reported as descriptive only and no primary verdict is claimed. The seed count is never reduced or extended because of outcomes.

primary.definition: D(cell) = align05_once loss at N_M minus random loss at 3000 in that cell, per seed (both at charged cost 3000). E_count = 1/2 x [(D(c) - D(a)) + (D(d) - D(b))] per seed, i.e. doubling the QA count (256 to 512 at share 1/16; 512 to 1024 at share 1/8) with the share held fixed, at exact equal cost. Mean over 24 seeds with a paired seed-bootstrap 95% interval (seed 8003, 10000 resamples, quantiles 0.025 and 0.975). Negative means a larger equal-cost advantage with more useful chunks.

secondary: Paired seed-bootstrap 95% intervals, no multiplicity adjustment, none changes the primary verdict: (1) D(cell) for each cell; (2) E_share = D(c) - D(b) (same 512 QA chunks at share 1/16 vs 1/8); (3) decomposition of E_count and E_share into a filter part (computed on align05_once loss at N_M alone) and a random part (random loss at 3000 alone), sign convention D = filter - random; (4) checkpoint-robust versions: D, E_count and E_share computed on the mean loss over the three cost points 2400, 2700, 3000 for each arm, and separately at 2400 and at 2700; (5) accuracy versions of D, E_count and E_share at cost 3000; (6) QA share and QA count of the kept sets per cell; QA chunks drawn and distinct QA chunks seen by random at each cost point; (7) random at 3000 minus no update, each cell; (8) realized cost: per cell, mean of (scoring seconds + sum of filter step seconds) minus sum of random step seconds, as a check of the charged-cost model; (9) loss spikes: per arm and cell, the number of runs in which the loss at 2700 exceeds both the 2400 and 3000 losses by more than 0.1, descriptive; (10) block consistency: E_count in block 1 and block 2 separately, descriptive only; (11) comparison with stage 79, descriptive: D(c) and D(d) against the stage-79 values (same pools, filter at 1633 vs N_8192 near 1574), and E_count against the stage-79 fixed-N (-0.083) and exact-equal-cost (-0.047) estimates.

prediction.written: Before any stage-80 code or run, 28 November 2026.
prediction.reasoning: Stage 79 gave E_count = -0.083 with N fixed and -0.047 [-0.116, +0.035] when the M = 4096 random arm was shortened to exact equal cost; both estimates are negative and the count effect came from the filter part (-0.110), not the random part (+0.027). In this stage the M = 4096 filter instead spends its unused budget on about 635 more one-pass updates, almost all on web chunks (it already keeps 95-98% of the QA chunks at N = 1633). Stage 75 suggests that adding mostly web chunks to a one-pass kept set gives little benefit, so the extra updates are expected to change the M = 4096 filter loss less than the stage-79 shortening changed the random loss. The direction of E_count is therefore expected to stay negative. With 24 seeds the interval half-width is expected to be about half of stage 79's (stage 79: about 0.065 to 0.075 at 97.5% with 6 seeds; here roughly 0.03 to 0.04 at 95%), so an effect near -0.05 would probably be detected and one near -0.02 probably not. This item rests on moderate evidence: the stage-79 exact-cost estimate included 0, and the effect of the extra M = 4096 filter updates has not been measured. Magnitudes are speculative and not part of the tested prediction.
other_items: D(cell) < 0 in all four cells, each with its 95% interval below 0.
Kept QA count of align05_once above 0.85 x Q in every cell (mean over seeds).
Decomposition of E_count: its filter part is the larger, i.e. |filter part| > |random part|.

decision_rule.supported: 95% interval entirely below 0: at fixed share and exact equal cost, more useful chunks increase the equal-cost advantage of one-pass filtering in this setting.
decision_rule.not_established: 95% interval includes 0: no claim about a count effect at exact equal cost; the estimate and its interval are reported.
decision_rule.refuted: 95% interval entirely above 0: at fixed share and exact equal cost, more useful chunks reduce the equal-cost advantage, contrary to the prediction.
decision_rule.other_items: Each other prediction item is reported as held or not held exactly as written; a failed item is not reinterpreted. The secondary contrasts, the checkpoint-robust versions and the block-wise estimates do not change the primary verdict.

resumption: Append-only JSON-lines journal outside the repository (/content/stage80-journal/journal.jsonl); completed (seed, cell, arm) entries skipped; population, pools, target and schedule digests re-verified on restart; outcomes not printed or read before the run finishes. After the calibration and every finished run the runner copies the journal and run log to branch colab/stage80-journal (results/stage80-interim/), commits and pushes, retrying a failed push once. A run interrupted before its journal line is written is restarted from step 0 with the same schedule; a completed run is never rerun. Resuming on another L4 follows blocks.machines.
audit: tools/audit_llm_exact_cost_count.py, written as for stage 79: journal digest; summary recomputation; environments (one or more, all L4) and step-0 identity across seeds and machines; calibration, the N_8192 and N_4096 bounds and the cost-point update counts; 192-run grid, block membership and order; schedules per seed and pool size; update counts and checkpoints; kept sets recomputed from journaled scores and their digests; QA shares and counts; random-arm QA draws; views per chunk; data and model hashes; the four pools rebuilt with digests equal to stage 79; target eligibility recomputed (criteria (a)-(e), counts) and the 512 target IDs re-drawn; target disjoint from all 3,840 exposed and 4,946 trained IDs. On an L4: recompute the proxy scores of seed 38000 in cells a and d; replay the first 50 steps of random and align05_once in cell a to their adapter digests for seed 38000 (block 1) and seed 38012 (block 2).
exposure: No new ArabicMMLU item is trained and no FineWeb-2 chunk outside the stage-79 pools is trained. The 512 new target items are evaluated and recorded as exposed in data/evaluation_status.json after the run (4,352 exposed test items in total). Pool chunks trained for the first time in this project (the M = 4096 kept sets are larger than in stage 79) are recorded by document index.
time_estimate: From stage 79 on an L4 (72 runs from 20:41 to 03:43 UTC, about 351 s per run; calibration c_r 0.1086 s, S(8192) 154.9 s, S(4096) 79.5 s; mean measured step 0.110 s for random and 0.111 s for the filter; one 512-item evaluation about 34 s; other per-run overhead about 19 s). Per run, both arms take about 330 s of scoring and training by design (exact equal cost), plus about 19 s overhead and 3 evaluations (about 102 s): about 450 s. Per seed: 8 runs plus one step-0 evaluation, about 61 min. Block 1: calibration and setup about 0.3-0.7 h (0.7 h if data, pools and target eligibility are rebuilt on a fresh machine) plus 12 seeds about 12.1 h, about 12.5-13 h. Block 2: setup about 0.5 h plus about 12.1 h, about 12.5 h. Total about 25 h of L4 time. This is longer than the 10 h per block assumed in planning: the 192 training runs alone take about 18.6 h, and the extra checkpoints cost about 3.6 h (two extra evaluations per run). With a single checkpoint per arm each block would take about 10.3 h.
licenses: As stage 79: FineWeb-2 ODC-By 1.0; ArabicMMLU CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial research use); Qwen2.5 Apache-2.0. No dataset text is committed; journals hold indices, scores and digests only.
scope: One trained model, one proxy, LoRA, one budget, two pool sizes, two shares, four cells (the stage-79 pools), one task scored by answer loss, 24 seeds, a fresh unexposed target. Count, share and pool size are linked (Q = M x s), so pool size per se is not separated. The filter's update count differs between pool sizes by design (exact equal cost), so the count effect is measured at equal cost, not at equal update count. Without random_once, the matched-selection term (filter vs a random subset of the same size trained once) is not measured in this stage. The useful chunks are in-format items from the target benchmark itself, as stages 74-79, so the stage measures how the amount of in-distribution data in web noise changes the equal-cost advantage, not a general capability gain.
